subject: Mutual plan: GPU pool phasing & commitment milestones
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual plan: GPU pool phasing & commitment milestones

Hi Chris —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I sketched a starter MAP focused on capacity lead times and commit milestones so Acme can be confident about Dedicated/Private delivery for the upcoming POC and production ramp. Key open items are lead-time tolerances for Dedicated vs Private, the minimum committed pool you need for a 3-month POC, and preferred phasing (POC -> pilot -> prod).

Attached: a short MAP PDF and a preliminary sizing workbook (redwood_gpu_sizing_v3.xlsx) with three scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive). Can you confirm:
- Which scenario best reflects your expected Q1 usage?
- Any contractual constraints on start/stop windows (e.g., procurement approvals that would delay a Nov start)?

I looped Aditya for sizing details and Marissa for the commercial cadence. If this looks OK, we propose the timeline below:

Proposed (high level)
- Week 0: MAP sign-off + contract sent
- Week 2-6: Dedicated pool provisioning (depending on region/hardware)
- Week 6-10: Private deployment (if requested, on-prem prep + airgap)
- Month 2-3: Pilot validation + scale to prod pool

Next steps: if you can share which scenario maps to your Q1 traffic we’ll firm up the GPU count and a firm procurement lead time.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: map-draft-acme-20261101.pdf (PDF, 12 pages); redwood_gpu_sizing_v3.xlsx (Excel, workbook)

Subject: Re: Mutual plan: GPU pool phasing & commitment milestones

Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear draft. High-level answers below:
- We expect the "expected" scenario is closest to reality for Q1 (approx 1.2M tokens/day at peak, ~40 concurrent inference lanes).
- Procurement: our purchasing cycle is unusual this year — internal approvals usually take 3 weeks but our CFO is out until Nov 22; if we need a signed master agreement before provisioning, that pushes earliest start to early Dec.
- We will likely request a private deployment for the pilot due to data residency concerns.

A couple of asks: can you call out nondisruptive fallback options if Dedicated provisioning slips? Also please call out lead times separately for A100-class vs L40-class hardware — our hardware team prefers pricing on both.

Best,
Chris
Head of AI Platforms
Acme Robotics

Subject: Re: Mutual plan: GPU pool phasing & commitment milestones — sizing notes

Chris / Stephanie —

Quick sizing + fallback notes based on the "expected" scenario (1.2M tokens/day peak, 40 concurrent):

Sizing (expected)
- Latency target: 150-200ms p95 for chat-like request patterns.
- Model family assumption: open LLM ~70B with fp16 or q4 quant profiles.
- Dedicated pool recommendation: 8 x L40s (steady state) with burst to 12 for peak windows OR 10 x A100s if you prefer denser A100 packing.
- KV caching + prefix caching expected to reduce token compute by ~25% for repeated prompts.

Lead times
- L40-class: provisioning typically 3–5 weeks in our US region (depends on inventory and rack scheduling).
- A100-class: 4–7 weeks (sourcing and burn-in longer).
- Private (on-prem): we estimate 6–10 weeks for site readiness + install (networking, KMS integration, airgap validation).

Fallbacks
- Soft fallback: auto-route a portion of traffic to hosted shorter-latency models (smaller family) with traffic steering policy; preserves availability but increases per-token cost.
- Hard fallback: enable temporary Dedicated burst on our shared pool for 2–4 weeks while private capacity completes (requires a short-term overcommit fee).

I attached a short workbook with per-GPU throughput and cost assumptions. If you confirm the scenario, I’ll produce a committed pool sizing table with month-by-month token and GPU projections for the MAP.

—Aditya
Sr. Infra SRE, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_gpu_sizing_v3.xlsx (see A tab: throughput), cost-estimates-q4.csv (CSV)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acme-robotics.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual plan: GPU pool phasing & commitment milestones — commercial / MAP cadence

Chris / team —

Following up on the MAP and Aditya's sizing notes. For the commercial cadence we propose the following commitment structure to enable Dedicated ordering while keeping your spend flexible:

Proposed commercial MAP
- Phase 1 (POC): 3-month minimum commitment at 50% of steady-state pool (4 L40s or 5 A100s) — discounted rate A.
- Phase 2 (Pilot): month-to-month ramp with an option to convert to a 12-month reserved pool with a 15% commit discount.
- Phase 3 (Prod): 12-month reserved pool (finalized after pilot) with SLA and priority capacity allocations.

Timing notes:
- If we need provisioning before Nov 22 (CFO return), we can provision into a short-term flex pool but require a PO / sign-off to proceed.
- DocuSign: I'll send a MAP addendum and a short SOW that rings in the GPU commitment and billing milestones.

Question for Acme: would you prefer the POC billing to be on a monthly invoice or net-30 with a PO?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acme-robotics.com>

Subject: Re: Mutual plan: GPU pool phasing & commitment milestones — commercial / MAP cadence

Marissa / team —

Thanks, this is helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. Quick confirmations:
- We’ll sign the MAP addendum and SOW. Procurement has asked for a PO-based billing cadence for POC (net-30 PO). Expect CFO back 22 Nov; aim to have the SOW in DocuSign by Nov 24 so we can issue a PO the week of Nov 29.
- Hardware preference: we will start with the L40 profile and keep the option to convert to A100 at conversion to reserved pool.
- Private deployment requested for the pilot. We will circulate a short security checklist to Priya for KMS and network configs.

Please send the DocuSign links and a one-page runbook for the private install window. Once we have the SOW we’ll route it to procurement.

Regards,
Chris
